transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you start by telling me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um… I guess work has been getting a little harder lately. I’m a cashier, and I’ve been having these moments at the register where I sort of… get stuck doing something that doesn’t really fit what’s happening. Like tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting.

It’s embarrassing, and I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but last week I got written up for it, so I thought maybe I should come in and talk to someone. Does that make sense?

When you find yourself tapping the scanner in that pattern or freezing over the drawer, does it happen because you feel a strong urge or worry that something bad will happen if you don't do it, or does it just happen suddenly on its own without you thinking about it first?

It doesn’t really feel like I’m doing it because I think something bad will happen, no. It’s more like… I’m at the register and then I just get stuck in it, if that makes sense. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just sort of hovering over the cash drawer while the person is waiting.

I know it looks odd, and I’m not trying to be difficult. It just kind of happens before I’ve really thought it through. Last week it got me written up, which was… embarrassing.

Right before the tapping or freezing happens, do you notice any kind of building tension or urge in your body that gets relieved once you do the movement, or does it just happen out of nowhere without any warning sensation?

I don’t really notice a buildup, no… not like tension that goes away afterward. It’s more that I’m just doing my cashier stuff and then I kind of get stuck—like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just pauses over the cash drawer even though the customer is waiting.

I know that sounds strange. I don’t mean to make a big deal of it, but it’s been noticeable enough that I got written up last week, so… I guess it’s not nothing. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed these tapping or freezing episodes happening throughout your life since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

No, not since I was a kid. This is more recent… as an adult. I’d say the voices and the more clearly out-of-place moments have been going on for about the last three months or so.

I mean, I may be making it sound worse than it is, but that’s about when I started noticing it more. Is that the kind of timeline you mean?
You mentioned 'voices' a moment ago—can you tell me more about that? Are you hearing sounds or voices that other people don't seem to hear?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days I hear what seems like a couple of people talking kind of off to the side of me.

Sometimes it’s like someone calling my name from the stockroom, or saying I rang something up wrong. And I’ll turn to check, because it sounds real enough, but there’s nobody there… and other people don’t seem to have heard anything.

I know that probably sounds strange. Is that what you mean by voices?

Over these past three months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or lacking energy, or alternatively times when you felt unusually elated, full of energy, or needed much less sleep than usual?

Um… I don’t think so, not in any big way. I mean, I’ve been stressed and kind of tired from work and all this, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had stretches where I felt hopeless or couldn’t get out of bed.

And I haven’t had the opposite either—like feeling unusually great or needing hardly any sleep. At least, not that I’ve noticed. I’m not sure if that’s helpful, but I don’t think my mood has been the main thing.
Have you had any recent illnesses, head injuries, seizures, or been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these episodes and voices started?

I don’t think there’s anything obvious like that. I haven’t had, um… a head injury or seizures that I know of, and I can’t think of a recent illness that lined up with it.

As far as drugs or alcohol or new medications… I don’t really have anything to point to there. I mean, if there’s something specific you’re asking about, I can try to think harder, but nothing is jumping out at me. Does that answer it okay?
During these freezing episodes, if someone tried to move your arm or reposition you, would your body resist or stay stiff, or would you just remain still without any noticeable resistance?

I’m not totally sure about the resisting part… I don’t think anyone’s really tried to move my arm, at least not that I remember.

It’s more like I just get stuck for a moment doing something that doesn’t really fit—like at the register I’ll be tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. Last week it actually got me written up, which is… embarrassing.

So I guess I’d say I just remain still, not that I’m stiff or pushing back. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Thinking back, do you recall any subtler changes—like feeling unusually suspicious, having trouble concentrating, or feeling 'off' in a hard-to-describe way—that started before these last three months, even if the voices and freezing themselves only became obvious more recently?

Yeah… I guess if I’m being honest, it didn’t just come out of nowhere three months ago. I didn’t really want to make too much of it, but I’ve felt kind of… off for a while.

Maybe about two years, a little more—since my youngest left the Eastern Shore for college. Two years and four months, something like that. I thought it was just the house being quieter or me adjusting, you know? I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
During these freezing spells, do you ever stop speaking or maintain an unusual body position for a long time, even if someone tries to talk to you or get your attention?

Not for a really long time, I don’t think. It’s more… I get stuck in the middle of what I’m doing at the register, like tapping the scanner in a pattern or just holding my hand over the cash drawer when the customer is standing there.

I can usually hear that someone’s trying to get my attention, but I don’t always snap out of it right away. It’s embarrassing more than anything. Last week it got me written up, so… I guess it’s noticeable. Is that answering what you mean?
During these episodes at the register, do you ever find yourself completely unable to speak or unwilling to respond at all when someone talks to you, or do you always eventually answer or react?

I don’t think I’m completely unwilling to answer, no. It’s more like I get caught in the thing I’m doing—tapping the scanner, or just sort of stuck with my hand over the cash drawer—and there’s a delay before I react.

I can usually come back and answer eventually. It just looks bad because the customer is waiting, and I know it doesn’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing. That’s the part that got me written up last week. Does that make sense?
Aside from hearing the voices, have you found yourself believing that people—like coworkers, customers, or others—are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you in some way?

I don’t think anyone’s trying to harm me, no. I mean… I get self-conscious at work sometimes, like if I mess up or freeze up, I wonder if people noticed or if they’re annoyed with me. But I don’t know that I’d say I believe they’re watching me or talking about me in that way.

Maybe I worry about it more than I should, but I haven’t really… seen anything definite, if that makes sense.

Besides these freezing and tapping episodes, have you ever found your body settling into an unusual position on its own, or noticed times when you felt overly restless or driven to move around a lot without a clear reason?

Not really like my body takes some strange pose on its own, no. And I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around for no reason.

It’s more the register thing I mentioned… I get stuck doing something that doesn’t really fit the moment, like tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or I freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is just standing there. I know that sounds odd. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything, it just happens, and last week it was enough that I got written up.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When these tapping or freezing episodes happen at the register, are you usually hearing the voices at that same moment, or do the episodes occur even when you're not hearing anything unusual?

It’s… not always exactly at the same time, I don’t think. But a lot of days I do hear things around then, yes.

It’s usually like a couple people talking just off to the side of me, or sometimes I’ll hear my name from the stockroom, or someone saying I rang something up wrong. And then I turn and there isn’t anybody there, or no one else seems to have heard it.

I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it does throw me off, and then I can get stuck or start tapping. Is that the kind of connection you mean?
Have you or others noticed that your speech sometimes becomes hard to follow—like jumping between unrelated topics, or using words in ways that don't quite make sense to others?

I don’t think so, not in a major way. I mean, I might lose my train of thought or answer awkwardly if I’m nervous, but I haven’t had people tell me I’m not making sense or that I’m jumping all over the place.

If anything, I probably try to keep my answers short so I don’t come off wrong. Does that answer what you’re asking?
